main_logic: Flood is measured as local depth above component datum, in m, depth at the pathway termination, in m, depth above the module lower edge, in m and flow velocity or scour proxy, in m/s.
Piecewise depth-damage points per part, set by engineering judgment from DOE/FEMP solar flood guidance and NEMA water-damaged equipment guidance, in the USACE depth-percent table form.
Why this shape: flood electrical damage is state/threshold-like by local component datum, so piecewise depth-percent curves are more auditable than logistics.
The damage ratio is a share of the replacement value of the same part (its own value bucket), never total project value.

steps.name: What it covers
steps.meaning: The parts that have a curve, their share of the value, and what has none yet
steps.fact: 8 parts with a curve · 3 without one yet
paragraphs: Flood on solar farms: piecewise depth-damage points per part, set by engineering judgment from DOE/FEMP solar flood guidance and NEMA water-damaged equipment guidance, in the USACE depth-percent table form. It names 8 parts: Inverters, Switchgear, Main transformer and controls, Combiner boxes and DC protection, SCADA and monitoring cabinets, AC and DC collection cable, PV modules and Foundations. Outside its scope: yearly and tail loss metrics (computed by the consumer, not the cell) and part values and exposure fractions (supplied by the consumer; not embedded in the curve file). Kinds of damage it does not include: flood duration, salinity and contamination (flags only, no numeric effect), energised versus shut-down state at flooding (flag only), water reaching equipment through conduits when the cabinet itself is above water (flag only, no multiplier) and debris impact on modules.

For this hazard the solar farm is split into 8 parts: Inverters, Switchgear, Main transformer and controls, Combiner boxes and DC protection, SCADA and monitoring cabinets, AC and DC collection cable, PV modules and Foundations. Parts of the plant's value with no curve yet: mounting and racking structure (debris and velocity load is a candidate mechanism; no curve), civil works: roads, access and fencing (reviewed in the write-up; no curve) and site drainage and flood defences (treated as protection state, not a damaged part).
The damage ratio is a share of replacement value of the same part (its own value bucket), never total project value. The files state no plant-level dollar figure for this asset.

steps.name: How it was derived
steps.meaning: How the hazard is measured, the shape of the curve and why that shape, and the site adjustments
steps.fact: 4 hazard measures → a line through points
paragraphs: Damage is read against local depth above component datum (m), depth at the pathway termination (m), depth above the module lower edge (m) and flow velocity or scour proxy (m/s). The curve is a line through fixed points (piecewise linear). The input, in the catalogue's words: water surface elevation or site flood depth (m), turned into local depth above each part's critical elevation, 0 to 2 m (clamp or warn); foundations use flow velocity (m/s) or a scour proxy, 0 to 4.

The adjustments — which selectors and conditioners change the curve — are written in the dossier; no seven-step audit table exists as a file. A site-condition adapter has not been written for this cell.
